description: Bounded exact minimum-weight cycle basis for connected simple undirected graphs using Horton candidates.

source.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm to Find the Shortest Cycle Basis of a Graph
source.author: Joseph D. Horton
source.candidate_construction: Mehlhorn and Michail, Minimum Cycle Bases: Faster and Simpler, https://people.mpi-inf.mpg.de/~mehlhorn/ftp/MinCycleBasisFasterSimpler.pdf
source.copyright: The publications remain copyrighted; this package uses algorithmic ideas and independently authored contracts, references, fixtures, and ports.

input.edge_count_range: N-1 through 12, also bounded by N*(N-1)/2
input.graph: connected, simple, undirected; each edge has 0 <= u < v < N; edge pairs are strictly increasing lexicographically

output.meaning: minimum total edge-weight, summed over all cycles in a GF(2) cycle-space basis; a tree has basis weight zero

algorithm_details.primary: For each root, construct a deterministic shortest-path tree with Dijkstra. For each graph edge not in that tree, XOR the two root paths and the edge to form a Horton candidate cycle. Deduplicate candidates, sort by (cycle weight, edge-mask), and use GF(2) Gaussian elimination to greedily select independent cycles until the cycle-space dimension M-N+1 is reached.
algorithm_details.independent_oracle: Enumerate every simple cycle by DFS with its least-numbered vertex as the start, deduplicate its edge mask, sort all cycles by weight, and run the cycle-space greedy basis extraction.
algorithm_details.tie_rules: Dijkstra uses perturbed edge lengths weight*(M+1)*2^M + 2^edge_id. A simple path suffix sum is below 2^M, and a whole basis suffix sum is at most M*(2^M-1), so this scale preserves the original minimum basis weight while selecting unique shortest paths. Candidate and cycle sorting uses unperturbed (cycle weight, unsigned edge mask).
algorithm_details.termination: At most N*M Horton candidates are considered; a connected graph has cycle-space dimension M-N+1. The bounded edge-mask fits in 12 bits.
algorithm_details.arithmetic_bound: A simple cycle weighs at most 8*9=72. Maximizing (min(12, N*(N-1)/2)-N+1)*9*N over N=3..8 gives a safe total bound of 378; distances, cycle weights, and totals use signed 64-bit integers.
